title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 23-24
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 23 to 24 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'गुरुर्गुरुतमो धाम सत्यः सत्यपराक्रमः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 23 to 24 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 23 to 24.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 23 to 24** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **गुरुर्गुरुतमो धाम सत्यः सत्यपराक्रमः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**गुरुर्गुरुतमो धाम सत्यः सत्यपराक्रमः । निमिषोऽनिमिषः स्रग्वी वाचस्पतिरुदारधीः ॥** **अग्रणीर्ग्रामणीः श्रीमान्न्यायो नेता समीरणः । सहस्रमूर्धा विश्वात्मा सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् ॥**

He is the Guru of gurus and the supreme abode. Truth is he, and truth is his strength, that God of gods. He blinks and never blinks, wears garlands, is lord of speech, and is noble of mind. He walks ahead of all, leader of the community, glorious is he. Justice itself, the guide, the form of the wind, is that God of gods. The Self of the universe with a thousand heads, eyes and feet is he.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 23 to 24 mean?
faq.a: He is the Guru of gurus and the supreme abode. Truth is he, and truth is his strength, that God of gods. He blinks and never blinks, wears garlands, is lord of speech, and is noble of mind. He walks ahead of all, leader of the community, glorious is he. Justice itself, the guide, the form of the wind, is that God of gods. The Self of the universe with a thousand heads, eyes and feet is he.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
